clue.text: Court cards?

parts.note: the clue looks like the picture cards of a pack, but a card is also a wag or comic, and the court here is a royal household's, where such comics were kept to amuse the monarch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court cards' are the kings, queens and knaves of a pack; read instead 'card' as a funny person, and the court as a royal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing joker, and the comics kept at a medieval royal court were its professional fools.

clue.text: Mozart symphony Holst thought jolly?

explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's Symphony No 41 carries this nickname; in Holst's suite The Planets, the same planet is subtitled 'the Bringer of Jollity'.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet's name is the nickname of Mozart's last symphony, and Holst's Planets suite labels that planet the bringer of jollity.

clue.text: Light dressing of stucco, say?

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the adhesive strip put on a small cut; the second reads the phrase literally, since stucco is a plaster that sticks to walls. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive bandage strip for a small wound is a light dressing, and stucco is wall render that clings, a plaster which adheres.

clue.text: Compound reciprocal pronoun in the Horace translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a new form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammarian spots a particular pronoun in an English version of Horace's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' fits the Latin poet Horace, but here it signals that THE HORACE is rearranged; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase expresses a mutual relation between subjects, so grammar books call it a compound reciprocal pronoun.

clue.text: Long -suffering sort in cot is disturbed

indicators.note: something disturbed is jumbled out of its order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient type is lying in a cot that has been disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges COT IS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Stoic philosophy endures hardship without complaint, so the word is used for any patient, uncomplaining person.

clue.text: Formic remedy for dyspepsia

explanation.walkthrough: Formic acid was first got from ants (Latin formica), so 'formic' describes an ant's acid; read as one word it is also an indigestion tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Formic acid is the sting chemical of the ant, and a stomach-settling tablet neutralises acid to ease indigestion.

clue.text: Adopts a facing position, making speeches

explanation.walkthrough: A golfer addresses the ball by taking up a stance facing it; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a stance squarely before the ball in golf is to address it, and formal talks to an audience are also called addresses.

clue.text: Strained and imperfect, possibly

explanation.walkthrough: The imperfect is a grammatical tense, so it is an example of the second sense, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut nerves are tense, and in grammar the imperfect is one of the verb forms showing time, a tense.

clue.text: Marks parts of logs

explanation.walkthrough: In mathematics a logarithm has a whole-number part, the characteristic, and a decimal part, the mantissa; the 'logs' are logarithms, not wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguishing traits are marks of a person, and the integer part of a logarithm is called its characteristic.

clue.text: Norfolk's ground, for example

parts.note: Norfolk here is not the English county but the Duke of Norfolk, and the ground is the territory or rank belonging to that title

explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county, but the clue means the Duke of Norfolk, England's senior duke, and his domain.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and territory held by a duke, such as the Duke of Norfolk, is his duchy or title.

clue.text: Kind performance, playing Hamlet

indicators.note: playing suggests the stage, but here it means the letters are played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentle actor gives a sympathetic performance in the role of Shakespeare's tragic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges KIND PERFORMANCE; Hamlet is Shakespeare's Danish prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is titled The Tragedy of Hamlet with this title, naming the hero as heir of the Danish throne.

clue.text: Capital approved, put into toy repair

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, so these words signal one piece placed inside another
to repair something is to rework it, so the letters of the word toy are rearranged

parts.note: OK means approved or agreed

explanation.surface: Approval is given in the capital for mending a broken toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges the toy's letters to TYO, and 'put into' sets the approval sign inside, after the T; 'Capital' at the front is the definition, not a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's seat of government is this city, so it is a capital.

clue.text: County cold at first — flat as a consequence

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
level means flat
and can mean 'and so', introducing a result

explanation.surface: A county is cold at the start of the year, so its landscape is flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' says C comes at the front. Cleveland was an English county from 1974 to 1996, round Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: This area of north-east England was an administrative county for two decades, a county.

clue.text: Men with spreads hear scorn poured out

indicators.note: something poured out is spilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big landowners listen as contempt is heaped on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' means large ranches, not butter or food; 'poured out' rearranges HEAR SCORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is American slang for a large farm, and the men who own or work such ranches are ranchers.

clue.text: Improves make-up with brushes again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to brush is to touch lightly

explanation.surface: Someone improves their make-up by applying the brushes once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'make-up' suggests cosmetics, but here it is the composition of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch up a picture or a face is to improve its appearance with small corrections.

clue.text: Corporation lawyer opens with single piece of information

indicators.note: the lawyer piece opens the word, coming before the other piece

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
corporation is old British slang for a pot belly, and tum is a belly

explanation.surface: A company lawyer starts a meeting with one fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but in British slang it is a large belly, TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is one fact or figure, the singular of data.

clue.text: Now opening church after ten years of corruption

parts.note: a decade is ten years

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church is opened now after ten years of moral rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the church last; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral decline or decay, a state of corruption.

clue.text: Spice escapade?

explanation.walkthrough: A caper is a pickled flower bud used as a seasoning, and a caper is also a playful escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: The bud of the caper bush is pickled as a seasoning, and a prank or frolic is also called a caper.

clue.text: Milk container put up by shy proprietor?

explanation.walkthrough: A coconut holds milk; a coconut shy is a British fairground stall where balls are thrown to knock coconuts off stands, which the stall owner sets up.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical nut is filled with a milky liquid, and fairground shy owners set such nuts on posts as targets.

clue.text: Transmitted experimental pictures of cricket eccentrics

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A broadcaster sends out trial pictures of oddball cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. A test card was the still picture TV channels showed when not broadcasting programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters transmitted a still trial image to check reception, called a test card.

clue.text: Small lumberjack a hard worker

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a logger fells trees, a lumberjack

explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who slogs keeps toiling, so a slogger is a diligent toiler.

clue.text: Piaf, for example, in France — thence USA, travelling

indicators.note: travelling letters move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Edith Piaf leaves France for a tour of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges THENCE USA. Edith Piaf was a French singer, and this is the French word for a female singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf was a celebrated female singer, which French calls a chanteuse.

clue.text: Bromidic elements of nitrites?

indicators.note: elements are parts of the whole, so the letters come from inside the word

explanation.surface: Chemists find the parts of nitrite compounds dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' suggests chemistry, but here it means a run of letters inside NITRITES.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a tired platitude, so bromidic means hackneyed and stale.

clue.text: Poet's licence to pre-elude in law

indicators.note: poetic licence takes liberties with words, so the letters are taken out of their order

parts.note: the word poet's, including its s

explanation.surface: A poet's freedom to anticipate events is confirmed in law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licence' rearranges POETS. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop someone is to bar them from asserting something contrary to what they said or did earlier.

clue.text: Record order in nightclub

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
O is an abbreviation for order, as in honours

explanation.surface: Records are played in order at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Downing Street, in that reform yet?

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Is Downing Street, in that political reform, still standing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges DOWNING, ST and IN THAT. Downing Street is the UK prime minister's address in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words concede a point while continuing, meaning 'nevertheless' or 'despite that'.

clue.text: Jack achieves ambitions

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives tar
to get is to achieve

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; here it is a sailor, TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims or goals one hopes to hit are ambitions.

clue.text: One cheers as pair hold rent

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lease is a rental agreement, so lease means rent

explanation.surface: Someone raises a cheer as a couple keep up the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'One cheers' means one who cheers people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings delight and gratification to others is a crowd-pleaser.
